transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Liam. Could I get your account number and PIN to pull up your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Liam, sure, account is 552-118-604, PIN 3391. This is Rachel Cortez.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks Rachel, that matches, you're verified. What can I help with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our streaming box in the living room keeps losing its WiFi connection, it buffers constantly and drops out completely a couple times an hour. Started a few days ago, right in the middle of shows.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, so the living room streaming box has been buffering and fully disconnecting a few times an hour for the past few days, usually mid-show. That's a frustrating one, especially when it cuts out right at the good part.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly, my kids have been asking why the TV keeps freezing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the kind of thing that gets old fast with a household depending on it. Let's get this sorted. I'm going to have you unplug the router for a moment, that usually clears up intermittent drops like this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, how long should that take before things are back to normal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It shouldn't take too long.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, unplugging it now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's back on, all the lights look normal.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, can you try streaming something now and see how it holds up?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, pulling up a show now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It played for a bit but just buffered again, so that didn't really fix it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that tells us it's probably not just a router hiccup. Let's dig a bit deeper. How many other devices are usually connected to the WiFi at the same time as the streaming box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Quite a few honestly, two laptops, three phones, and a smart speaker.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, and is the streaming box on WiFi or connected with an ethernet cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on WiFi, we never ran a cable to that room.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it. Has anything changed recently, any new devices added around when this started?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually yes, we got a new gaming console a few days ago, around the same time this started.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a useful lead, gaming consoles can pull a lot of bandwidth, especially during downloads or updates. Is it in the same room as the streaming box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, right next to it actually, same shelf.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, let's check the WiFi channel congestion then, when several devices crowd the same channel it can cause exactly this kind of buffering and dropout. Give me a moment to check that from our side.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see your router's on a pretty congested channel right now, likely from your neighbors' networks as well as your own devices. I'm going to switch it to a clearer channel and enable band steering so newer devices like the console default to the less crowded 5 gigahertz band.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that makes sense, we never touched that setting ourselves.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, it's usually something that needs adjusting on our end. Let me apply that now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Done, that's applied. Let's test again, can you stream something now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, trying now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's playing smoothly, no buffering at all this time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's great to hear. So the fix was really about clearing the channel congestion, the extra devices, especially the new console, were crowding the same frequency as the streaming box and causing the drops.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes a lot of sense, appreciate you actually finding the cause instead of just having me unplug things over and over.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is that channel congestion something that could come back if we add more devices later?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's possible, especially if a lot of new devices join at once, but band steering should help spread newer ones onto the clearer band automatically going forward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, that's reassuring.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. Now, just to log this properly, which room was the affected device in again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The living room, the streaming box, same as I said at the start of the call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, sorry, I've got that noted, living room streaming box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No worries. Should I keep an eye on it for a while, or is this pretty much confirmed fixed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'd keep half an eye on it for the rest of today just to be safe, but the channel change directly addresses what we found, so I'd expect it to hold.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sounds good, I'll let the kids know it should be back to normal.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. If it does act up again, mention the channel change was already made today so whoever you reach doesn't have to start from scratch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do, that's a good tip. Is there anything else I should watch for with the new console, or was this really just the one setting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: This was really just the one setting for this particular symptom. If you add even more devices down the line, it's worth having us check channel congestion again, but for now this should hold steady.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got it, that's good to know for planning ahead.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more thing, is there a way to get an alert if the connection drops again, or would we only notice from the TV freezing like this time?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unfortunately nothing automatic on our end for that specifically, you'd notice it the way you did this time, through the stream buffering.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, fair enough, at least we know what to check now if it happens again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, and the account notes will have today's fix documented, so it'll be quick to reference if you do call back.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. I think that covers it for today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Anything else I can help with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything, thank you Liam.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Rachel. We do value your feedback, so please stay on the line after this call for a short survey. Thank you for choosing S-Net, have a great rest of your day.
